findings.reason: a node following this clause records a "verified checkpoint" on a test that the empty-archive case passes, so the plan's whole protection for §4 rests on a guard that does not inspect the thing it is protecting.
findings.text: §3's done-when requires that "its archive passes an integrity test of the whole stream, and the same test fails on a deliberately truncated copy", but a whole-stream integrity test validates the gzip stream and says nothing about the archive's contents: an archive whose `graph.dump` member is present and zero-length passes it, and the negative control (truncating the stream) exercises only the truncation case, so the guard fires for the one failure mode it tests and stays silent on the one the repository's own criterion was written for — `imas_codex/graph/AGENTS.md` and `imas_codex/graph/neo4j_ops.py:514` define a verified recovery archive as "a gzip tar containing a non-empty `graph.dump` member", and the export path produces that member by `cp` from `$DATA_DIR/dumps/neo4j.dump` (`imas_codex/graph/remote.py:944`), so a failed dump yields a well-formed stream carrying nothing

findings.reason: this comparison is the section's newest and least self-evidencing claim; without a recorded before/after pair the run in §4 proceeds on an unverifiable statement that the store survived intact, and the evidence_paths rule asks exactly for such evidence on a durable path.
findings.text: the clause §3 changed adds "a read afterwards returns the same node count as the read taken before the stop", but the clause names a recorded location only for the archive test and its truncated-copy failure ("both recorded under `docs/evidence/fragments/sn-full-dd-continuation/`"), leaving both node counts unrecorded — so the equality is asserted with no receipt a later reader or the §4 node (which is required to read the graph "with no graph writer running" after this checkpoint) can open, and a restored graph that came back short leaves nothing behind showing what it was measured against
